events.headline: High-Speed Train Collision Near Urda, Spain, Kills at Least 68
events.summary: A high-speed train rear-ended a stopped train near Urda, Toledo, on Oct 28 after a signaling failure improperly cleared it to proceed, killing at least 68 people and injuring about 58. Prime Minister Sánchez declared three days of national mourning.

events.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro Flees Brazil for US After Election Loss, Defying Passport Order
events.summary: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil after Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes barred him from international travel and ordered him to surrender his passports following Lula's runoff win. He crossed into Argentina on foot and flew to Miami; the US State Department said it will grant him and his family visas.

events.headline: Tibet Earthquake Death Toll Holds at 16 as Search Operation Concludes
events.summary: The death toll from the magnitude 7.0 earthquake in Tibet's Baqen County remains at 16, with injuries revised up to 76 and no missing persons reported. More than 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds were damaged or destroyed, and over 12,000 people have been evacuated to 18 shelters.

events.headline: Vucic Concedes Defeat as Students' List Wins Decisive Majority in Serbian Election
events.summary: President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat on Oct 25 after 14 years in power as the Students' List movement won a decisive majority of roughly 135-142 of 250 seats. Turnout reached about 70%, the highest since 1992, with celebrations breaking out in Belgrade.

events.headline: Israeli Election Produces Deadlocked Knesset, Record Arab-Party Turnout
events.summary: With about 90% of votes counted in Israel's Oct 28 election, Netanyahu's bloc holds 53 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc 48, both short of the 61 needed for a majority. Arab-majority parties surged to a combined 19 seats, their strongest showing in years, leaving no clear path to government formation.

events.headline: Sudanese Army Drone Strikes on RSF-Held Markets Kill Over 200 Across Two Attacks
events.summary: Sudanese Armed Forces (not RSF, as initially reported) drone strikes hit two RSF-held markets: one on Oct 18-19 at a transport hub in West Kordofan killing an estimated 80-110 people, and another on Oct 19-20 at the Amiet market in the Abyei border region killing 150 or more and displacing about 8,000. South Sudan summoned Sudan's ambassador in protest and the UN condemned the strikes; local civic groups' higher estimate of around 150 for the first strike remains unconfirmed.

events.headline: Ethiopia Severs Ties With Eritrea as Border Fighting Escalates Over Tigray Rebel Support
events.summary: Ethiopia closed its Asmara embassy and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats on accusations Eritrea is arming Tigrayan rebels; Eritrea responded by severing diplomatic ties. The Tigrayan EPFAS rebel alliance struck Addis Ababa military facilities on Oct 1, and Eritrean troops near Zalambessa came under Ethiopian drone attack as fighting advanced toward Idaga Hamus, marking the worst flare-up since the 2018 peace deal.

events.headline: DR Congo's Ebola Outbreak Tops 10,000 Cases and Nearly 4,900 Deaths
events.summary: DRC's Bundibugyo-virus Ebola outbreak, declared in May 2026, has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases and about 4,887 deaths, a 48.6% case-fatality rate, making it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record and the fastest-growing. Cross-border cases have been confirmed in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria and France, and no approved vaccine exists for this strain.

events.headline: Drone Strike on Nyala Market in South Darfur Kills at Least 36
events.summary: A Sudanese Armed Forces drone strike hit a market in RSF-held Nyala on Oct 26; MSF confirmed at least 36 killed and more than 150 injured. A rights group and the RSF-aligned local health ministry reported unverified higher tolls of 100 to 188.

events.headline: Machado Says She Is Ready to Meet Venezuela's Interim President Rodríguez
events.summary: Two days after returning from exile, opposition leader María Corina Machado said on Oct 26 she is willing to meet interim president Delcy Rodríguez 'with full transparency and an agenda' to discuss a democratic transition. Rodríguez dismissed Machado's return as a 'show.'

events.headline: Qatar Presents Iran With New Draft Deal to End War With US; Iran Calls It Unacceptable
events.summary: Qatari mediators presented Iran around Oct 25-28 with a draft proposal for a seven-day confidence-building timeline to end the US-Israel-Iran war. A senior Iranian official called the plan 'unacceptable,' while Trump has not ruled out renewed strikes after the Nov 3 US midterms.

events.headline: US Strike on Suspected Drug Boat Kills 5, Southern Spear Toll Tops 240
events.summary: On Oct 27, US Southern Command struck a boat in the Eastern Pacific alleged to be trafficking drugs, killing five people with no cargo evidence presented. The 'Southern Spear' campaign has now killed at least 240 people in more than 70 strikes since September 2025.

events.headline: El Salvador Deploys 1,000 Troops to Haiti Searching for Missing Soldiers
events.summary: Four Salvadoran Air Force technicians went missing Oct 18 after a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince. El Salvador deployed roughly 1,000 additional troops and special forces to search for them, with President Bukele warning of a stronger response if they are not returned unharmed.

events.headline: North Korea Positions Howitzers Facing South Korea Along DMZ
events.summary: North Korea has deployed self-propelled 122mm howitzers visibly facing south along the DMZ, with soldiers conducting fortification and fencing work reported around Oct 27. The move follows months of rising tension since a September DMZ mine blast wounded three South Korean soldiers.

events.headline: Bangladesh Measles Outbreak Kills Over 1,200 Children Since March
events.summary: The WHO confirmed a nationwide measles outbreak affecting 58 of Bangladesh's 64 districts since mid-March 2026, with more than 1,200 child deaths by October. WHO assessed the national risk as 'high,' with the outbreak rooted in vaccination disruptions following 2024 political unrest.

events.headline: Houthis Claim New Strikes on Saudi Oil Pumping Stations and Riyadh Airport
events.summary: On Oct 26, a Houthi spokesman claimed fresh drone attacks on Saudi East-West crude pumping stations and a missile strike on Riyadh airport, a day after a larger barrage targeting multiple Saudi cities. Saudi authorities and Aramco gave no official confirmation of damage.

events.headline: Cyclone Arnab Makes Landfall in Andhra Pradesh, Kills at Least 7
events.summary: Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Narasapuram, Andhra Pradesh, in the early hours of Oct 28 with sustained winds of 125-135 km/h and a storm surge of 1.5-2.5 meters. The death toll climbed from an initial three to seven or eight by Oct 29, with more than 180,000 people evacuated across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

events.headline: Localized Ceasefire in Oleshky Brokered by Melania Trump Takes Hold
events.summary: A localized ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky, Kherson Oblast, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, began taking effect Oct 27 to allow humanitarian aid and evacuation of about 1,700 mostly elderly residents. The Vatican disputed credit, saying the Pope's direct calls with Putin and Zelensky were central to the deal.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrikes Kill Civilians in Sagaing, Damage Historic Monastery
events.summary: Myanmar junta forces conducted about 30 airstrikes in Sagaing Region, killing five civilians and injuring 23, and damaging a historic Buddhist meditation center. The junta claims the operations serve peace efforts despite continued civilian casualties.

events.headline: Russia Launches Major Missile and Drone Barrage on Kyiv; Ukraine Strikes Russian Plants
events.summary: Russia fired about 16 ballistic missiles and up to 280 drones at Kyiv overnight Oct 26-27, killing at least one person, injuring up to 16 and damaging infrastructure. Ukraine retaliated with drone strikes on Russia's NLMK steelworks in Lipetsk and an Azot chemical plant in Novomoskovsk, sparking fires.

events.headline: Ethnic Clashes Near Moyale Drive 36,000 Across Ethiopia-Kenya Border
events.summary: Oromo-Somali clashes around the border town of Moyale, triggered by a flag dispute, have killed at least nine people and driven about 36,000 people across the border into Kenya as of Oct 28.

events.headline: China's Q3 GDP Grows 4.5%, Beating Forecasts, on Export Surge
events.summary: China's economy grew 4.5% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, up from 4.3% in the second quarter, driven by a 36.3% export surge in September. Retail sales rose just 1.1%, underscoring weak domestic consumption and a continued decline in property investment.

events.headline: UK Announces Record £10 Billion Ukraine Support Package
events.summary: The UK announced an additional £10 billion package for Ukraine on Oct 28, comprising £7 billion in economic support and export finance over three years plus £500 million in urgent winter military and air-defense aid. It is described as the UK's largest-ever Ukraine package, bringing total commitments to about £35 billion.

events.headline: Nigeria-Origin Ebola Patient Evacuated to Switzerland
events.summary: On Oct 26, a Swiss woman confirmed as Nigeria's first Ebola case since 2014 was medically evacuated to Geneva University Hospital, with her husband isolated at Zurich University Hospital. Officials said there is no risk to the Swiss population.

events.headline: China Withdraws Mandarin Teachers From Philippine Schools Amid Tensions
events.summary: China withdrew between 150 and 180 Mandarin teachers from Philippine Chinese-community schools starting Oct 1, after the Philippine defense secretary warned of security risks from such exchanges. The move is tied to broader escalating Philippines-China friction in the South China Sea.

events.headline: Afghan Taliban Mortar Fire Kills Civilian, Wounds Five in South Waziristan
events.summary: Afghan Taliban mortar fire killed one civilian and wounded five others in a border clash in South Waziristan on Oct 27. Pakistan responded by destroying Afghan border posts.

events.headline: Takaichi Cabinet Approval Hits New Low Amid Agriculture Minister Scandal
events.summary: A Jiji Press poll found Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi's cabinet approval fell to 42.4%, its lowest since she took office, following Agriculture Minister Kazuo Yana's resignation over alleged funding violations. Other polls diverge sharply, with Kyodo showing 49.1% and Nikkei showing 62%.

events.headline: Netherlands Confirms €1.2 Billion Non-Military Aid to Ukraine Through 2029
events.summary: During a visit by President Zelensky, the Dutch government announced on Oct 28 €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) in non-military aid for Ukraine through 2029 to support energy, water infrastructure and reconstruction, plus a separate €500 million military aid package including air defense and drones.

events.headline: Bomb Blast Near Colombia-Venezuela Border Bridge Injures Police in Cúcuta
events.summary: A bomb exploded on Oct 27 near the Francisco de Paula de Santander International Bridge in Cúcuta, Colombia, injuring four to seven police officers outside a tax-agency office; no deaths were reported. The bridge was closed and the blast follows the assassination of a former city official a day earlier.

events.headline: Brussels Rejects US-Russia Push to Reopen Nord Stream Pipeline
events.summary: The European Commission said on Oct 28 that Nord Stream will not be allowed to bring Russian gas into Europe after the war ends, rebuffing a US-Russia effort to revive the pipeline. It cited EU law phasing out Russian pipeline gas by September 2027.

events.headline: Cuba's Guiteras Power Plant Suffers Fifth Failure of October
events.summary: Three simultaneous boiler failures hit Cuba's Guiteras power plant in Matanzas on Oct 27-28, the fifth such failure this month, taking the plant offline for an estimated four more days and deepening the national blackout crisis.

events.headline: IMF Cuts Argentina's 2026 Growth Forecast to 2.1%
events.summary: The IMF's October World Economic Outlook cut Argentina's 2026 GDP growth forecast to 2.1% from 3.5%, while raising its inflation forecast to 32.5% and unemployment to 7.6%, even as it continued to back President Milei's economic reforms.

events.headline: Mexican Navy Kills Guasave Cartel No.2 'Chuy' González in Sinaloa Shootout
events.summary: Mexican naval forces killed Jesús 'Chuy' González Peñuelas, the Guasave Cartel's second-in-command, during an Oct 26 operation in Sinaloa after his group opened fire on navy personnel; two people died in the clash. González was wanted by the US DEA with a $5 million reward.

events.headline: Students Protest in Jakarta Over Prabowo's Forest-Fire Response
events.summary: More than 1,000 students and activists protested in Jakarta on Oct 28, with further protests in Bandung and Makassar, criticizing President Prabowo's handling of Indonesia's worst forest fires and haze in 11 years and demanding spending be redirected to disaster response. More than 14,000 security personnel were deployed in Jakarta.

events.headline: Suspected Drone Strike Hits Container Ship Off Bulgaria's Black Sea Coast
events.summary: Three maritime drones struck a container ship sailing from Haifa to Constanța off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast on Oct 28; all 18 crew members were rescued unharmed. Suspicion has fallen on Russia, though no group has claimed responsibility.

events.headline: Europe Records Its Worst-Ever West Nile Virus Season
events.summary: The ECDC reported 1,715 locally-acquired West Nile virus cases across 19 EU countries as of October 2026, the highest number ever recorded, including the first-ever local transmission in Belgium. Italy was worst-hit with 748 cases.

events.headline: Egypt Shuts Down Mada Masr, Convicts Editor Lina Attalah
events.summary: On Oct 27, a New Cairo court convicted Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah of running an unlicensed website, fined her about $54,000, and ordered the independent outlet's closure. CPJ, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International condemned the ruling as a press-freedom blow.

events.headline: H5N1 Avian Flu Outbreaks Confirmed in Poultry Across Cambodia, India, Taiwan
events.summary: New H5N1 avian influenza outbreaks have been confirmed in poultry across Cambodia, India and Taiwan, with Cambodia also reporting one human case who has since recovered.

events.headline: Germany's Ifo Business Climate Index Hits Highest Level Since 2023
events.summary: Germany's Ifo Business Climate Index rose to 90.2 in October 2026, its sixth consecutive monthly rise and the highest level since May 2023, driven by improved business expectations.

events.headline: Tanzania Announces Major Gas Discovery in Mnazi Bay
events.summary: Tanzania's Energy Minister announced on Oct 27 the discovery of about 223 billion cubic feet of natural gas in the Mnazi Bay block near Mtwara via the Kasa-1X ST2 well, the country's first new gas discovery in more than a decade. Production is expected to begin around November 2026.
